definitions.full: H7883. Shichor שִׁיחוֺר proper name, of a river on border of Egypt, probably east branch of Nile ; — ׳הַשּׁ Josh 13:3 , ׳שׁ מִצְרַיִם 1Chr 13:5 ; clearly = Nile, שִׁחֹר זֶרַע Isa 23:3 (|| קְצִיר יְאוֺר ), שִׁחוֺר מֵי Jer 2:18 ; compare Dl Pa 311 Wilson Hast. DB SHIHOR (usually derived from I. שׁחר , as black water , but doubtful).
definitions.rootNote: or שִׁחוֹר ; or שִׁחֹר ; probably from 7835 ; dark , i.e. turbid ;

occurrences.englishText: from the Shihor, which is before Egypt, even to the border of Ekron northward, which is counted as Canaanite; the five lords of the Philistines; the Gazites, and the Ashdodites, the Ashkelonites, the Gittites, and the Ekronites; also the Avvim,
So David assembled all Israel together, from the Shihor the brook of Egypt even to the entrance of Hamath, to bring God’s ark from Kiriath Jearim.
On great waters, the seed of the Shihor, the harvest of the Nile, was her revenue. She was the market of nations.
Now what do you gain by going to Egypt, to drink the waters of the Shihor?
